subject: Architecture
title: The Sydney Opera House: A Decade of Drama
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Sydney Opera House: A Decade of Drama usable.

hook.text: The Sydney Opera House was budgeted at $7 million. It cost $102 million.

buildup.text: Jørn Utzon's shell-shaped roof was so complex that no engineer knew how to build it.

discovery.text: Utzon realized every shell could be cut from a single sphere, making prefabrication possible.

twist.text: The government fired Utzon before it was finished. He never returned to see the completed building.

climax.text: The Opera House became a UNESCO World Heritage Site and Australia's most recognized symbol.

punchline.text: They fired the genius. Then put his building on every postcard.

quiz.question: How did Utzon solve the problem of building the Opera House shells?
options: He used flexible steel cables to shape each shell
He cut every shell shape from a single sphere geometry
He abandoned the original design for flat panels
